relevance.rationale: A personal-recollections essay written for Gerry Brown's 85th birthday, not a technical paper: it narrates the development of chiral EFT nuclear forces from the author's vantage. It has already been read into the corpus once — docs/audits/2026-08-02-t3-writhe-vs-delta-lambda-sign.md lines 149-153 record that it 'corroborate[s] the same Pauli-principle spin-isospin correlation; no additional sign structure beyond the exchange symmetry was found', i.e. an honest negative. Reading it again confirms that: the only reusable technical content is Fig. 4 and its surrounding paragraph (p.6), which restates the Weinberg-counting hierarchy that library/arxiv-0811.1338v1/0811.1338v1.pdf gives more authoritatively and in more detail. It is therefore a corroborating secondary source for a statement the corpus already has from a better source, and no result in it is load-bearing anywhere. Recording it as supporting rather than tangential only because a durable audit doc cites it by bare arXiv id and that citation should resolve.

keyResults.statement: Three-nucleon forces appear only two orders after the dominant NN forces, and four-nucleon forces are further suppressed, appearing only at N3LO — presented as the Weinberg power-counting diagram hierarchy for the 2N/3N/4N effective potential.
keyResults.useForFolio: A second, independent statement of the k-body hierarchy already taken from Epelbaum-Hammer-Meissner. Its only use is corroboration: it lets the GAP-9 framing cite two sources for the ordering rather than one, which matters because the ordering is what makes the mu_4 comparison meaningful.

proposedActions.rationale: A durable audit doc cites it by bare arXiv id with no ref() entry. One entry closes that dangling citation. Low priority — the technical content is fully covered by 0811.1338. Suggested id meissner2010chiral (note: distinct author from the existing meissner2004 entry, which is Krzysztof A. Meissner on loop-quantum-gravity BH entropy — do not collide the keys).
